title: Three untested crypto ideas on existing / freely fetched data: USDT premium, ETH-BTC Coinbase premium spread, Weiss on every Friday
registered: 2026-10-20, before any Gen249 number (USDT-USD fetched from Coinbase's public API, 2021-05..)

A_usdt_premium.signal: Coinbase USDT-USD hourly close; d = close - 1; p24 = 24h mean of d (min 20); z = (p24 - 720h mean) / 720h sd (min 480), as the Coinbase-premium zc; read at the 23:00 UTC bar. z > 1 -> long BTC and ETH 0.25 each, z < -1 -> short 0.25 each, held the next UTC day
A_usdt_premium.why: buying crypto offshore needs USDT; paying above $1 for it signals fresh USD demand (like the Coinbase / kimchi premia, which work)

B_eth_btc_premium_spread.signal: s = zc_ETH - zc_BTC (Gen108 Coinbase premium z per coin, 23:00 UTC); z = (s - 30-day mean) / 30-day sd (min 20); z > 1 -> long ETH 0.25 / short BTC 0.25, z < -1 the reverse, held the next day
B_eth_btc_premium_spread.why: relative US demand between the two coins; market-neutral, so low correlation with the directional sleeves

C_weiss_every_friday.rule: the Weiss expiry sleeve (fade the 07-08 UTC move from 08:00 to 10:00) applied on EVERY Friday (Deribit weekly expiries too), replacing the last-Friday-only sleeve; same costs, same half weight
C_weiss_every_friday.why: the hedging-flow mechanism applies to every expiry; weekly expiries are smaller, so the per-event effect may be smaller but there are 4x the events (the monthly version has t = 1.6 on 81 events)

pass: v7 (perp costs): sleeve DEV > 0, TEST >= 0.8, HOLD >= 0.5, corr C* <= 0.3 (A, B) AND strict rule vs v7 (2.534 / 3.494 / 2.240). bf2 (CFD costs): sleeve DEV > 0, TEST >= 0.5, HOLD >= 0.3 AND strict rule vs bf2 uncapped (2.378 / 3.699 / 2.118). C is judged on the books only (it replaces a sleeve).
